terms.definition: The broad, flat, green part of a plant that makes food by capturing sunlight.
terms.function: Carries out photosynthesis to make food for the plant.
terms.whereItIs: Growing from the stem out into the sunlight.
terms.whyItMatters: The leaf makes the food that feeds the plant and nearly all life.

terms.definition: The process by which a plant uses sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide to make sugar and release oxygen.
terms.function: Makes the plant's food and releases oxygen into the air.
terms.whereItIs: Happens mainly in the green cells of the leaf.
terms.whyItMatters: It is how plants feed themselves and produces the oxygen we breathe.

terms.definition: The green pigment in plant cells that captures energy from sunlight.
terms.function: Absorbs sunlight so the plant can make food.
terms.whereItIs: Inside chloroplasts, mostly in the leaf.
terms.whyItMatters: Without it the plant could not capture the light energy it needs to make food.

terms.definition: Tiny tubes running through a leaf that carry water in and food out.
terms.function: Deliver water and minerals in and move food out to the rest of the plant.
terms.whereItIs: A branching network across the whole leaf.
terms.whyItMatters: Veins connect the leaf to the plant's water and food transport system.
